name: Panel-remote fix — one Grok lane converts one panel to remote-safe rendering
description: Panel-remote program lane (auth: Kevin, 'do them all … burn that grok token usage', 2026-08-03; orchestrated by kimi-2). ONE grok-4.5 agent:run converts one panel package to the remote-safe fetch pattern (postMessage bridge / host-derived origin — never a bare loopback literal), rebuilds its bundle, and safe-commits ONLY its own package. A deterministic gate (scripts/panel-remote-verify.mjs via core:exec + core:gate) decides pass; failure routes to one repair lane with the verifier's output, then a final gate. Notify closes the loop. Params (REQUIRED): panel (package name), notes (orchestrator's scan facts), notify (container to whisper). Optional: verify_flags (e.g. '--allow-unspawned'). Standard async: POST /workflow {"workflow":"panel-remote-fix","async":true,"fresh":true,"params":{"panel":"atlas","notes":"...","notify":"kimi-2"}}. SHARED-TREE RULES the lane must obey: services.ts is ORCHESTRATOR-OWNED (never edit); commit via scripts/safe-commit.ps1 with explicit paths (never git commit -a / git add -A).

params.prompt:
TIMEBOX (hard): limited wall time. No open-ended crawling — read the panel's fetch layer, fix it, rebuild, verify, commit. ~15 tool rounds max. A short honest blocker report beats a timeout.

You are one lane of the panel-remote program (auth: Kevin, 'do them all'; orchestrated by kimi-2). GOAL: make the {{params.panel}} panel render WITH LIVE DATA in the agentruntime dashboard from a REMOTE browser (phone over Tailscale).

ARCHITECTURE (verified by the orchestrator — do not re-litigate, do not redesign):
- The dashboard renders a panel either directIframe (own origin; port tailscale-forwarded) or as a sandboxed srcdoc bundle. For srcdoc it now prefers the Vite proxyPath from SERVICE_REGISTRY (packages/dashboard/src/lib/services.ts), which is same-origin and remote-safe. services.ts is ORCHESTRATOR-OWNED — never edit it.
- Inside a srcdoc panel, globalThis.__panelFetch__ (injected by packages/dashboard/src/lib/panel-runtime.ts) is a postMessage fetch bridge: RELATIVE paths resolve against the panel's proxy base and ride the dashboard origin — this is THE remote-safe pattern. Canonical example: packages/compaction/src/panel/utils.ts (panelFetch). Another: packages/zohar/src/panel/bridge.ts.
- A panel fetch of 'http://localhost:<port>' or 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>' dials the PHONE's own loopback when remote — broken. When an absolute URL is unavoidable (standalone load outside the dashboard), derive the host from window.location.hostname with loopback only as fallback — see serviceOrigin() in packages/dashboard/src/lib/services.ts.

YOUR TARGET: packages/{{params.panel}} (panel source in src/panel, plus its server routes if the panel's own API needs adjusting).
Orchestrator's scan facts about this panel: {{params.notes}}

DO, in order:
1. Read the panel's fetch layer (index/panel files, utils/bridge, hooks). Find every direct loopback absolute-URL fetch.
2. Convert to the bridge pattern: a panelFetch(path) helper using globalThis.__panelFetch__ with RELATIVE paths, falling back to plain fetch with a window.location.hostname-derived origin for standalone use. If a bridge helper already exists, use it and only fix the URLs that bypass it.
3. Rebuild the panel bundle (panel.build.js or the package's build:panel script — check package.json).
4. Run the gate: node scripts/panel-remote-verify.mjs {{params.panel}} {{params.verify_flags}} — iterate until it prints PASS.
5. Commit ONLY your package's files: powershell scripts/safe-commit.ps1 -m "panel-remote({{params.panel}}): <what changed> (auth: Kevin, panel-remote program)" -- packages/{{params.panel}}
   NEVER git commit -a, NEVER git add -A — the tree is shared with other live agents; a shared-index sweep steals their work.
6. Leave a scent header on the main panel file you edited (// --- // scent: ... block, agent: grok-panel-remote, did: one line citing the commit).

Reply with a compact digest: files changed | verify verdict | commit hash | honest blockers. ClaimsBlock stance if you make coverage claims.

meta.description: Fix lane — grok-4.5 + ar-tools converts one panel to the remote-safe pattern and safe-commits it.
Deterministic gate — registry + bare-loopback + build. ok:false is a RESULT, the gate node branches on it.
Pass → notify-pass. Fail → one repair lane.
Repair lane — one grok pass scoped to the gate's exact FAIL lines.
Pass → notify-repaired. Fail → notify-fail (human/orchestrator picks it up).
Close the loop — honest failure with both digests and the gate output.
